- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to counteract pessimism.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 10–15 day horizon; apply a 1–2% upward bias for medium-term forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 3–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average smoothing.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, model fails to adjust; force a 1–2% downward correction in next 5-day window.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if model is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment history with alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → -0.50 → 0.33) triggers model instability; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to dampen forecast volatility.
